statement.p: Let T_n(x) be the n^{th} degree Taylor approximation of f(x) about x = 8.

p.alert: Use 4 decimal places in your two answers below, but make sure you carry all decimals when performing calculations.

statement.p:
T_{2}(10) is an
over
under estimate of f(10).
Using the Lagrange Error Bound for T_n(x), calculate:

solution.p: The n^{th} degree approximation of f(10) about x=8 is given by:
f''(x) is always negative in the interval [8,10] so T_{2}(10) is a underestimate of f(10).
Using the Lagrange Error Bound we find an M such that:
\left|f(10)-T_{2}(10)\right| \le \frac{M}{3 !}\left|10-8\right|^{3}, where M \ge \left|f^{3}(t)\right| for all t in the interval [8,10].
By examining \left|f'''(x)\right| we find that it is biggest when t=8. Therefore, a suitable choice is M=f'''(8).
